cards.a: Internal membranes that work together - some physically connected, others linked by vesicles.

cards.q: Name the parts of the endomembrane system.
cards.a: Nuclear envelope, ER, Golgi, lysosomes, vesicles and vacuoles, plasma membrane.
Tiny sacs made of membrane that move membrane segments between organelles.

cards.q: Why is the plasma membrane in the endomembrane system?
cards.a: It is linked to the other membranes by vesicle transfer.

cards.q: What is the largest part of the endomembrane system?
cards.a: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) - a network of flattened sacs and tubules.
Endoplasmic = 'within the cytoplasm'; reticulum = Latin for 'little net'.

cards.q: How is the ER directly connected to the nucleus?
cards.a: ER membranes are continuous with the nuclear envelope.

cards.q: How does the ER reach other organelles indirectly?
cards.a: Vesicles bud from the ER and travel to other parts of the system.

cards.q: Why does the ER enclose a space separate from the cytosol?
cards.a: It divides the cell into compartments, each able to keep different conditions.

cards.q: Which includes the rest: ER, vesicle, endomembrane system, nuclear envelope?
